subject: Cardiovascular
vignette: A 2-month-old infant born to a mother who drank heavily throughout pregnancy has growth restriction, a smooth philtrum, and a thin upper lip. A new murmur is heard on examination, and echocardiography is ordered to evaluate for congenital heart disease.
question: Which of the following sets of cardiac defects is most likely to be found in this infant?

options.text: Transposition of the great arteries and truncus arteriosus
VSD, PDA, ASD, and tetralogy of Fallot

explanation_correct: Prenatal alcohol exposure (fetal alcohol syndrome) is associated with VSD, PDA, ASD, and tetralogy of Fallot. The dysmorphic features described — growth restriction, smooth philtrum, and thin upper lip — identify fetal alcohol syndrome, and a new murmur in such an infant should prompt evaluation for these septal and conotruncal defects.

explanation_incorrect.A: Atrioventricular septal defect is the defect classically associated with Down syndrome, not fetal alcohol exposure.
explanation_incorrect.B: Ebstein anomaly is associated with prenatal lithium exposure and features downward displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets.
explanation_incorrect.C: Supravalvular aortic stenosis is the cardiac defect of Williams syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.D: Transposition of the great arteries, truncus arteriosus, and tricuspid atresia are associated with infants of patients with diabetes during pregnancy.

educationalObjective: Prenatal alcohol exposure is associated with VSD, PDA, ASD, and tetralogy of Fallot.

subject: Cardiovascular
vignette: A newborn has hypotonia, a flat facial profile, epicanthal folds, and a single palmar crease. Cytogenetic testing shows trisomy 21. A murmur is detected, and echocardiography reveals a defect in which the atrial septum and atrioventricular valves are abnormal.
question: Which congenital cardiac defect is most likely present in this infant?
explanation_correct: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) is associated with atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD), as well as VSD and ASD. The combination of dysmorphic features, trisomy 21, and a defect involving the atrial septum and atrioventricular valves identifies an AVSD, the classic cardiac lesion of Down syndrome.

explanation_incorrect.A: Coarctation of the aorta is associated with bicuspid aortic valve and Turner syndrome, not trisomy 21.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ebstein anomaly is associated with prenatal lithium exposure and involves downward displacement of the tricuspid valve leaflets.
explanation_incorrect.D: Supravalvular aortic stenosis is the cardiac defect associated with Williams syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.E: D-transposition of the great arteries is associated with infants of patients with diabetes during pregnancy and presents with early cyanosis from separate systemic and pulmonary circulations.

educationalObjective: Down syndrome is associated with AVSD (as well as VSD and ASD).

subject: Cardiovascular
vignette: A 1-week-old infant born after a first-trimester maternal illness with a fine macular rash and arthralgias has cataracts and sensorineural deafness. A continuous, machine-like murmur is heard at the left infraclavicular area, and echocardiography confirms a wide patent ductus arteriosus.
question: Which of the following additional cardiac defects is most likely associated with this infant's congenital infection?

options.text: Ebstein anomaly of the tricuspid valve
Pulmonary artery stenosis and septal defects

explanation_correct: Congenital rubella is associated with PDA, pulmonary artery stenosis, and septal defects. The triad of cataracts, sensorineural deafness, and a PDA with the classic continuous machine-like murmur identifies congenital rubella syndrome from the first-trimester maternal rash and arthralgias.

explanation_incorrect.A: Transposition of the great arteries is associated with infants of patients with diabetes during pregnancy and presents with severe early cyanosis, not with the cataract-deafness-PDA triad.
explanation_incorrect.B: Ebstein anomaly is associated with prenatal lithium exposure, involving downward displacement of the tricuspid valve leaflets.
explanation_incorrect.D: Atrioventricular septal defect is associated with Down syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.E: Bicuspid aortic valve and coarctation/dissection are associated with Turner syndrome, not congenital rubella.

educationalObjective: Congenital rubella is associated with PDA, pulmonary artery stenosis, and septal defects.
